questions.question: Who was the 24th Governor of the Reserve Bank of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Urjit Patel__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Urjit Patel was the **24th Governor of the Reserve Bank of India** from 4 September 2016 to10 December 2018.
 
• He had also served as **Deputy Governor of RBI** from 11 January 2013 to 4 September 2016.
 
• Presently he is the **Chairman** of **National Institute of Public Finance and Policy (NIPFP)** is an autonomous research institute under Ministry of Finance, Government of India.
 
• **Urjit Patel** was the** Chairman** of **Expert Committee to Revise and Strengthen the Monetary Policy Framework**, appointed by **RBI** on **September 12, 2013.**
 
 
• **Expert Committee to Revise and Strengthen the Monetary Policy Framework**:
 
 
• **Objective** of the Committee is to recommend what needs to be done to revise and strengthen the current monetary policy framework with a view to, inter alia, making it transparent and predictable.
 
• **Suggestion:** The Committee suggested a five-member **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)** - three members from the RBI and two nominated by the Government. 
 
 
 
• Presently the committee comprises six members - three officials of the RBI and three external members nominated by the Government of India.
 
 
• **The Governor of RBI is the ex officio chairperson of the committee**. 
 
• They need to observe a "silent period" seven days before and after the rate decision for "utmost confidentiality". Decisions are taken by majority with the Governor having the casting vote in case of a tie.
 
• The current mandate of the committee is to maintain **4% annual inflation until 31 March 2021** with an upper tolerance of 6% and a lower tolerance of 2%.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• He had also served as **Chairman** of the Prime Minister's **Economic Advisory Counci**l, from August 2009 to May 2014.
 
• He was the Chairman of the **Twelfth Finance Commission of India.**
 
 
 
• **Y V Reddy** was the **21st Governor of the Reserve Bank of India**.
 
 
• He was the chairman of the **Fourteenth Finance Commission of India.**
 
 
 
• **Bimal Jalan** was the **20th Governor of the Reserve Bank of India.**
 
 
• He has also been the **Chairman of the Economic Advisory Council** to the **Prime Minister** between January 1991 to September 1992.

questions.question: Vibration of which among the following produces only odd harmonics?

options.text: An air column in a closed organ pipe
A vibrating rod fixed at two ends
An air column in an open organ pipe
A vibrating string fixed at two ends

questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is **__An air column in a closed organ pipe__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a closed pipe, only **odd harmonics are produced.**
 
• The frequencies of harmonics are in the ratio of **1: 3: 5.....**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

__
 
• Each natural frequency that an object or instrument produces has its own characteristic vibrational mode or standing wave pattern. 
 
• **A harmonic is an integer** (whole number) multiple of the fundamental frequency.
 
• The harmonics generated depend on the note or chord being played, and each frequency will produce different harmonics.
 
• The harmonics heard are based on the fundamental frequency being played and produce a lower amplitude (or volume) as they increase from 1st to 8th harmonic.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **When a string is fixed at both ends,** two waves travelling in opposite directions simply bounce back and forth between the ends.
 
• This will produce even harmonics.
 
• **When air is blown into the open organ pipe,** the air column vibrates in the fundamental mode.
 
• Antinodes are formed at the ends and a node is formed in the middle of the pipe.
 
• The frequencies of harmonics are in the ratio of 1: 2 : 3...

questions.question: Standing in an open ground on a cloudless day, at what time will your shadow be the shortest?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**12:00.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• From sunrise to sunset, the sun traces an arc across the sky and reaches its highest point in the sky at local noon.
 
• As the sun moves through the sky, the shadow cast by an object is constantly changing in length.
 
• The** shortest shadow occurs when the sun reaches its highest point, at local noon.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Shadows are** longest in the early morning and late afternoon/early evening** when the sun appears low in the sky.
 
• As the Earth rotates on its axis, the sun hits each location in the morning at an angle.
 
• This makes the shadow appear long.
